scope: Read-only typographic diagnosis of final archived v10, not a mathematical-method revision
prior_qa_limitation: Earlier semantic equality, numbering and no-clipping checks were insufficient to certify typography. They did not test correct upright math text/operators, font substitution, relative sizing, matrix-column alignment, delimiter style or reading flow.

findings.issue: Operators and descriptive mathematical labels are italic or visibly expanded into separate letters in final PDF
locations: main p6 Eq7 dev and Eq8 argmin/lex
main p8 Eq11 min/argmin/rank and Eq12 Specificity
supp p2 S2 max, S4 corr/min, S5 CI/boot
supp p4 S11 std and S12 CPU/archive/all/max
findings.evidence: PDF page images show operator/label typography as italic letter sequences. Actual OOXML Specificity/argmin has m:sty=p, yet final PDF is italic, so the present style survives XML but not this renderer.
findings.recommendation: Use explicit upright identifiers and function-name/normal-text nodes, validate actual rendering. Test m:nor plus explicit w:i=false for textual runs; do not rely on font name or m:sty=p alone.

findings.issue: TP, FP, FN, TN are typeset as spaced italic mathematical letters rather than compact count abbreviations
locations: main p7 count-definition paragraph and Eq9
findings.evidence: Rendered TP reads T P, and all count labels are italic; source TeX also uses plain TP/FP/FN/TN as multiple mathematical variables.
findings.recommendation: Encode all four count identifiers as upright whole tokens, e.g. \mathrm{TP}, while retaining the same counts and formulas.

findings.issue: Supplementary formula base size does not match declared engine size and its surrounding prose/number
findings.evidence: PDF body prose is 11pt and equation numbers 11pt, while ordinary equation/inline-math letters are mostly 12pt. Scripts are mostly7.2pt and nested symbols down to about5.13pt. This is a readability/style mismatch, not a claimed BMT minimum-font violation.
findings.recommendation: Choose and validate a consistent 11pt or12pt math base in the exported PDF; use legible script proportions and avoid unnecessary nested scripts.

findings.issue: Long prose labels placed in math objects disrupt normal text and cause letter spacing
locations: supp p4 first paragraph: s in {benign,malignant}
supp p4 CPU/archive in replay definition
findings.evidence: benign and malignant appear as large italic letter sequences in a set inside prose; similar descriptive labels become spread-out superscripts/subscripts.
findings.recommendation: Keep long verbal definitions in ordinary prose; use short mathematical indices and compact upright labels where genuinely needed.

findings.issue: Dedicated math font setting is not reflected in final PDF fonts
findings.evidence: Despite DOCX mathFont and run fonts being Latin Modern Math, inspected PDF spans/fonts are LiberationSerif, OpenSymbol and NimbusRoman; no Latin Modern Math is embedded on these pages.
findings.recommendation: For DOCX use a conventional Word math font such as Cambria Math and verify compatibility, then configure/verify a suitable available rendering font for PDF. Font fallback alone is not always wrong, but it cannot be treated as proof that desired math typography was preserved.

findings.issue: All displayed equations are inline oMath plus tab stops; no oMathPara is present
findings.evidence: Inspected word/document.xml. The14/12 numbered groups use the same inline object type as prose, between tab runs. This is valid OOXML, but lacks a dedicated display-math container and is a compatibility/style risk.
findings.recommendation: Prototype proper display OMML, or a robust dedicated equation layout, keeping equation numbers at the right margin. Check native Word and exported PDF rather than only object count.

findings.issue: Intended aligned-column justification may be lost during import due property ordering
locations: main Eq1/2/7/9/10/12/13/14 and supplementary aligned groups
findings.evidence: Pandoc m:mcPr writes mcJc before count. Standard examples put count before mcJc. Current multiline equations show uneven left-column placement and excessive gaps, particularly Eq14/S11. This is a testable root-cause hypothesis, not established causation.
findings.recommendation: Prototype schema-order normalization count then mcJc and confirm right/left column alignment in rendered output; alternatively use equation-array alignment at the relation sign.

findings.issue: Automatic stretchy delimiters are visually oversized and thin in many short inline expressions
locations: main p5 inline box coordinates and clipping ranges
main p6 a(t), indicators and Eq8 tuple
supp p2 Wilson-bound notation and p3 sign tuples
findings.evidence: Short expressions show tall thin fences whose style differs from normal parentheses in surrounding text. They amplify the baseline/spacing mismatch.
findings.recommendation: Use fixed ordinary parentheses/brackets for short inline expressions; keep stretching for genuinely tall fractions/cases only.

findings.issue: Long inline count formulas and multi-definition rows are too dense for smooth reading
locations: main Eq14 and supp S11 first row
findings.evidence: The count paragraph contains four long math fragments with changing inline height; Eq14/S11 puts two definitions on a row then a much longer lhs on the next row.
findings.recommendation: Use a compact separate aligned count definition or plain prose for the counts; put common weight, standardized rate and difference on three relation-aligned rows within the same equation group.

findings.issue: Number alignment is generally sound and formulas are not currently clipped
findings.evidence: All numbers are at the right margin; no red parser placeholders or missing perturbation direction was seen in current archived v10. Formula content is semantically intact on the reviewed pages.
findings.recommendation: Preserve number positions and mathematical content while rebuilding typography. Do not reintroduce the already-fixed Eq2 red-placeholder issue.

acceptance_checks: Actual rendered operators min,max,argmin,rank,clip and textual labels are upright and compact.
TP/FP/FN/TN are whole upright count identifiers.
Main and supplementary math base sizes match the chosen document styles; scripts remain readable.
Short inline math aligns with surrounding text and does not contain expanded word labels.
Multiline groups align at relation signs without arbitrary column gaps.
Equation numbers remain at the right edge, without overlap or loss of content.
No red/error/tofu glyphs, and all brackets, signs and perturbation directions are present.
Inspect the final DOCX with a word processor and final PDF; do not infer appearance from OMML counts alone.
limitations: This audit directly observed the final PDFs and DOCX XML; it did not observe the user’s exact Microsoft Word/WPS environment.
The mcPr property-order explanation is a hypothesis for the rendering engine to test.
No scientific content, data, DOCX or build scripts were edited.
